                    [32m' *     onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login",\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   },\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * })\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export interface Auth extends AuthHooks {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Name of the Prisma model that represents the application user connected to\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * your business logic.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * The user entity needs to have an ID field that uniquely identifies each\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * user. It can be of any name and type, but it needs to be marked with `@id`:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * model User {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   id Int @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * You can add any other fields you want to the user entity. Make sure to also\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * define them in the `userSignupFields` field if they need to be set during\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * the sign-up process.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/entities) for how the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * user entity connects to the rest of the auth system.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    userEntity: EntityName;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Enabled authentication methods. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    methods: AuthMethods;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Route that Wasp redirects unauthenticated users to when they try to\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * access a page that has `authRequired: true`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Adding Auth to the Project](https://wasp.sh/docs/tutorial/auth#adding-auth-to-the-project)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * for an example.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Route that Wasp redirects users to after a successful login or signup.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m"     * Only takes effect when using Wasp's built-in Auth UI.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Auth UI](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/ui).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @default "/"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAuthSucceededRedirectTo?: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'interface AuthHooks {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before the user is created. Receives `providerId` plus the common\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * hook input. Throw from this hook to reject a signup based on custom\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * criteria.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onBeforeSignup?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called after the user is created. Receives `providerId`, the created\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * `user`, and, for social auth, `oauth` fields including tokens and the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * unique OAuth request ID.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAfterSignup?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Called once, after the user verifies their email. Receives `email` and `user`. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAfterEmailVerified?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before redirecting the user to the OAuth provider. Receives the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * generated `url` and `oauth.uniqueRequestId`. Return `{ url }` to override\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * the redirect URL.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onBeforeOAuthRedirect?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before the user is logged in. Receives `providerId` and `user`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Throw from this hook to reject a login based on custom criteria.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onBeforeLogin?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     * social auth, `oauth` fields including tokens and the unique OAuth request\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ID.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAfterLogin?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Enabled authentication methods for the app.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * At most one local auth method ({@link LocalAuthMethods}) can be used, but you\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * can enable as many external auth methods ({@link ExternalAuthMethods}) as you\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * need.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export type AuthMethods = RequireOneOrNone<LocalAuthMethods> & ExternalAuthMethods;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Built-in local auth methods.\n'[39m +

                    [32m' * delegates into `context.entities` and invalidate the client cache when\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * related actions modify them.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * See [Queries](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/operations/queries).\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @example\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```ts\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * import { app, query } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                    [32m" * import { getTasks } from './src/queries' with { type: 'ref' }\n"[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * export default app({\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   // ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   spec: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     query(getTasks, { entities: ["Foo"] }),\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   ],\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * })\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @param fn\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m" * Reference to the Query's NodeJS implementation.\n"[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * See [the\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * docs](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/operations/queries#implementing-queries)\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * for details on the implementation and its context.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * {@include ./referenceImports.md}\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @param config\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @category Constructors\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export declare function query(fn: Query["fn"], config?: QueryConfig): Query;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @inline\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @expandType Query\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'type QueryConfig = Omit<Query, "kind" | "fn">;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Creates an {@link Action} definition.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Actions are server-side write operations. Like queries, they can be\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * called from the client and the server. Listing entities in `config.entities`\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * lets Wasp invalidate related query caches when this action runs.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * See [Actions](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/operations/actions).\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @example\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```ts\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * import { app, action } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * import { createTask } from "./src/actions" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * export default app({\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   // ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   spec: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     action(createTask, { entities: ["Task"] }),\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   ],\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * })\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @param fn\n'[39m +
                    [32m" * Reference to the Action's NodeJS implementation.\n"[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * See [the docs](https://wasp.sh/docs/data-model/operations/actions#implementing-actions) for details on the implementation and its context.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * {@include ./referenceImports.md}\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @param config\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @category Constructors\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export declare function action(fn: Action["fn"], config?: ActionConfig): Action;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @inline\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @expandType Action\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'type ActionConfig = Omit<Action, "kind" | "fn">;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Creates an {@link Api} endpoint definition.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +

                    [32m" * them for webhooks, file uploads, or any HTTP interaction that doesn't fit\n"[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +

            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +

            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.).             [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: Replace <Share URL> with the Share URL from system information if available. If not available, omit the " | [Task](...)" part.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands\n'[39m +
            [32m'- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:\n'[39m +
            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'\n`[39m +
            [32m'Commit message here.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'🤖 Generated with [Pochi](https://getpochi.com) | [Task](<Share URL>)\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +
            [32m'EOF\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +

            [32m'IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Use the description/body for details, not the title\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed\n'[39m +

            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m`gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'\n`[39m +
            [32m'## Summary\n'[39m +
            [32m'<1-3 bullet points>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'## Test plan\n'[39m +

                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Build entries with the dedicated constructors ({@link page}, {@link route},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * {@link query}, {@link action}, {@link api}, {@link apiNamespace},\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * {@link job}, {@link crud}).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    spec: Spec;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Wasp compiler metadata used by the app.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export interface Wasp {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * The Wasp version this app is built for, as an npm-compatible\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * [SemVer range](https://github.com/npm/node-semver#ranges)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * (e.g. `"^0.24.0"`).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    version: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Authentication configuration and lifecycle hooks.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * See the [Auth overview](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/overview) for the\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * supported auth methods and how the `User` entity is connected to auth.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * If hooks are async, Wasp awaits them. All hooks receive `prisma` and `req`\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * in their input. Hook return values are ignored except for\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * {@link AuthHooks.onBeforeOAuthRedirect}, which can change the redirect URL.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * In TypeScript, you can type each hook implementation with its matching\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * type from `wasp/server/auth` (e.g. `OnBeforeSignupHook`). See\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * [Auth Hooks](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/auth-hooks) for the full hook\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * inputs and examples.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * @example\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```ts\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * export default app({\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   // ...\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   auth: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     userEntity: "User",\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     methods: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *       usernameAndPassword: {}, // use this or email, not both\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *       google: {},\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *       gitHub: {},\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     },\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *     onAuthFailedRedirectTo: "/login",\n'[39m +
                    [32m' *   },\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * })\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export interface Auth extends AuthHooks {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Name of the Prisma model that represents the application user connected to\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * your business logic.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * The user entity needs to have an ID field that uniquely identifies each\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * user. It can be of any name and type, but it needs to be marked with `@id`:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```prisma title="schema.prisma"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * model User {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *   id Int @id @default(autoincrement())\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * ```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * You can add any other fields you want to the user entity. Make sure to also\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * define them in the `userSignupFields` field if they need to be set during\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * the sign-up process.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Accessing User Data](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/entities) for how the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * user entity connects to the rest of the auth system.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    userEntity: EntityName;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Enabled authentication methods. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    methods: AuthMethods;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Route that Wasp redirects unauthenticated users to when they try to\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * access a page that has `authRequired: true`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Adding Auth to the Project](https://wasp.sh/docs/tutorial/auth#adding-auth-to-the-project)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * for an example.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAuthFailedRedirectTo: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Route that Wasp redirects users to after a successful login or signup.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m"     * Only takes effect when using Wasp's built-in Auth UI.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * See [Auth UI](https://wasp.sh/docs/auth/ui).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @default "/"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAuthSucceededRedirectTo?: string;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'interface AuthHooks {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before the user is created. Receives `providerId` plus the common\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * hook input. Throw from this hook to reject a signup based on custom\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * criteria.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onBeforeSignup?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called after the user is created. Receives `providerId`, the created\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * `user`, and, for social auth, `oauth` fields including tokens and the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * unique OAuth request ID.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAfterSignup?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /** Called once, after the user verifies their email. Receives `email` and `user`. */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    onAfterEmailVerified?: Reference<AnyFunction>;\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    /**\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * Called before redirecting the user to the OAuth provider. Receives the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * generated `url` and `oauth.uniqueRequestId`. Return `{ url }` to override\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * the redirect URL.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     *\n'[39m +
                    [32m'     * @category Hooks\n'[39m +
